thread:
marta: noticed a p99 jump for tenant acme-pro right after runtime v3.2 canary rolled at ~16:00 UTC. p95 up a bit too. no 5xxs, just heavy tails. anyone else seeing this?
riju: yup saw the same alert. p95 from ~120ms -> 290ms, p99 from ~420ms -> ~1.1s since 2024-11-02T16:02Z. queues spiking on hotpath.
sam: do we have a sample request id / flamegraph? any recent infra changes other than v3.2? @ops-bot did canary go to 12%?
ops-bot: deploy: runtime-v3.2 canary -> 12% completed at 2024-11-02T16:00:00Z.
marta: flamegraph: https://grafana.internal/redwood/perf/f/abc123. sample req: req_20241102_160205_acme. no 5xx, just queue_ms ballooning.
kbrown: repro steps I used locally (lightweight):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":32}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=redwood-7b-quant &
# run with 20 concurrent clients for ~30s
```
kbrown: when I run that against canary traffic split I see p99 ~1.0s, p95 ~280ms.
riju: digging traces now. seeing long alloc_wait / kernel-switch waits in the tail on the canary hosts.
sam: v3.2 introduced the "quant-scheduler" kernel selector change + a different allocator path for small-batches. sounds like allocator interaction is queuing.
marta: good hypothesis. can we bisect at the selector level? e.g., flip kernel selector back for suspect cohort or split by host pool.
kbrown: I can toggle a per-tenant feature-flag to force legacy-scheduler for acme-pro. doing it now.
kbrown: toggled legacy-scheduler for tenant=acme-pro at 2024-11-02T16:05:30Z. monitoring...
kbrown: p99 dropped from ~1.1s -> 320ms within a minute. p95 back to ~130ms. :thumbsup:
marta: nice, that isolates the problem to scheduler/allocator interaction.
sam: mitigation path: (1) narrow canary to 3% while we investigate host-level allocator, (2) push feature-flag to affected customers, (3) rollback scheduler change in next patch if needed.
riju: collecting heap/alloc traces from canary hosts and will run targeted repro with synthetic taily workload. adding links to trace snapshots here: https://traces.internal/trace/def456
sam: also add a p95/p99 alert keyed by kernel-selector tag so future rollouts alert quicker.
marta: I've created ticket PERF-3289 and linked the customer support ticket #3289 -> support-bot noted it.
support-bot: ticket #3289 annotated with mitigation (legacy-scheduler flag) and customer notified.
kbrown: logs snippet for the bad tail:
```
[2024-11-02T16:02:05Z] tenant=acme-pro req=req_20241102_160205_acme latency=1120ms queue_ms=850 kernel=quant-scheduler alloc_wait=620ms host=canary-17
```
kbrown: and after flag flip:
```
[2024-11-02T16:06:12Z] tenant=acme-pro req=req_20241102_160612_acme latency=320ms queue_ms=90 kernel=legacy-scheduler alloc_wait=40ms host=canary-17
```
riju: next steps: run a controlled sweep of kernel variants on a limited host set, add unit test for small-batch allocator path, and schedule a postmortem to decide whether to revert the v3.2 selector change or further tune allocator.
sam: assigning eng-runtime owners: @kbrown (mitigation), @riju (traces/bisect), @marta (customer comms + postmortem).
marta: will file postmortem + rollout checklist. leaving canary at 3% for now and feature-flag enabled for affected tenants. thanks all.
support-bot: update: customer acme-pro notified 2024-11-02T16:09:00Z, they confirmed improved latency.
marta: last note — keeping this thread open until bisect results are in. resolved-for-now at 2024-11-02T16:09:59Z.
